The relationship between the kinetic energy of electrons and the diffraction pattern
observed when they impinge on a crystal surface is fundamentally linked to the de Broglie
wavelength of the electrons. For a lattice spacing of 0.4 nm, the electrons must possess
sufficient kinetic energy to produce constructive interference, leading to observable
diffraction patterns. To achieve this, the energy level required is approximately 10 eV,
as this energy allows the electrons to have a de Broglie wavelength that is comparable to
the lattice spacing. When the kinetic energy of electrons is at this level, their
wavelengths are suitable for interacting with the crystal's periodic structure, resulting
in distinct diffraction patterns that can be analyzed to understand the material's
properties. Thus, the 10 eV energy threshold is crucial for observing the effects of
electron diffraction in crystalline materials.
answers.explanation: correct because the kinetic energy of electrons influences their de Broglie wavelength, which must match the crystal lattice spacing of 0.4 nm to produce constructive interference and observable diffraction patterns, with approximately 10 eV being the necessary energy to achieve this condition.

Replacing the Sun with a black hole of the same mass would not alter the gravitational
forces acting on the planets, and consequently, their orbits would remain unchanged. This
is because gravitational force depends solely on the mass of the objects and the distance
between them, as described by Newton's law of universal gravitation. Since the mass of the
black hole would equal that of the Sun, and its position would be the same, the
gravitational pull experienced by the planets would be identical to what they currently
experience. Thus, the planets would continue to orbit the black hole in the same manner as
they do the Sun, maintaining their existing orbital mechanics.
answers.explanation: correct because gravitational force is determined by the mass of the objects and their distance, and since a black hole with the same mass as the Sun would exert the same gravitational pull at the same location, the orbits of the planets would remain unchanged.
